fact: Justice Minister Ziyambi told Parliament that the programme begun in July 2025 requires all urban freehold stands, sectional titles and agricultural land to be digitised, with the Digital Land Administrative Platform to become the sole authoritative title register after the 24-month validation period ends in July 2027 (Open Parly).

The Masvingo Mirror reports title deeds are being digitised under the Presidential Deeds Digitisation Programme at US$200 each, with submissions since April 2026 and a digitisation deadline of mid-2027, though lawyers say no deed submitted has been returned.

NewsDay reports Zimbabwe launched a nationwide Title Deeds Validation and Securitisation Programme under S.I. 76 of 2025 to verify and digitise existing title deeds, announced by the Permanent Secretary of Justice.
The Permanent Secretary said conveyancers submit the title deed information through the DLAP system to the Deeds Registry for processing, after which a securitised title deed is issued.

Lawyer Vengai Madzima says 16 law firms were selected for a two-week pilot to test the Digital Land Administration Platform before full implementation, as the Deeds Registry moves away from paper under S.I. 76 of 2025 with a validation deadline around 18 July 2027.

The Department of the Surveyor General's eCadastre portal is live, described as a public record platform with land parcel boundaries, ownership and usage information, and lets users search property by district, owner name, property ID or deed number.
The eCadastre portal states property can be searched online from anywhere, with property cards available after payment, and surveyors can e-lodge surveys.
Zimbabwe launched the Digital Land Administration Platform for electronic processing of title deeds, per a Government Gazette notice announced by Justice Minister Ziyambi Ziyambi.
Justice Minister Ziyambi Ziyambi said the DLAP enables farmers and landowners to apply for title deeds online, alongside the manual process.
